hero.lead: A nation of 212.8 million that holds 58.5% of its land in forest, designed a global fund to keep forests standing, and still leaves half its people without a safely managed toilet.

stats.label: Committed to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility

capital.heading: Brazil has priced its forest for the world. Next, a safe home for every citizen.

record.text: Committed to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, the fund Brazil launched at COP30, after the Netherlands’ pledge in October 2026
Third sovereign sustainable bond, November 2025: 7 years at 5.75%, with orders of about $6.7 billion
Mobilised by Eco Invest Brasil in its first year, including R$46 billion from foreign investors
Foreign-exchange hedging made available by the IDB and the Central Bank of Brazil
World Bank support to the new Bolsa Família, the cash transfer that protects family incomes; about 9 million children expected to benefit

register.name: Euro bonds 2030, 2033 and 2036
register.detail: Priced 17 April 2026 · Settled 23 April 2026 · Coupons 4.000%, 4.875% and 5.500%
register.note: Three tranches · Order book above EUR 16 billion at its peak
register.text: Brazil returned to the euro market with three bonds: EUR 2.0 billion to 2030 at a yield of 4.240%, and EUR 1.5 billion each to 2033 at 5.031% and to 2036 at 5.627%. Peak demand was more than three times the amount issued. A second currency of borrowing widens the investor base behind the public budget that carries the seven standards.

register.name: Global 2036 bond and Global 2056 reopening
register.detail: Priced 9 February 2026 · Coupons 6.250% and 7.250% · Yields 6.400% and 7.300%
register.note: New 10-year bond of $3.5bn and a $1.0bn reopening · Order book about $12 billion
register.text: A new 10-year dollar bond of $3.5 billion maturing in May 2036 and a $1.0 billion reopening of the 2056 bond. Demand was about 2.7 times the amount issued. Sovereign bonds set the benchmark against which Brazilian borrowers, public and private, raise dollars.

register.name: Tropical Forest Forever Facility
register.detail: Launched 6 November 2025, COP30 Belém · Commitments as of October 2026
register.note: Total commitments after the Netherlands’ pledge of up to USD 500 million, October 2026
register.text: A fund launched by the Brazilian COP30 presidency to pay tropical forest nations for forest kept standing. USD 5.5 billion was announced at launch, with 53 countries endorsing the launch declaration.
by: Tropical forest nations and sponsor countries

register.name: Sustainable Global 2033 bond
register.detail: Priced 6 November 2025 · 5.500% coupon · yield 5.75%
register.note: Orders of about $6.7 billion, three times the amount issued
register.text: Brazil’s third sovereign sustainable bond, sold alongside a $750 million reopening of its 2035 bond. Proceeds are tied to the nation’s social and environmental spending under its sustainable bond framework.

register.name: Eco Invest Brasil
register.detail: Blended finance and currency protection · Auctions from 2024
register.note: Mobilised in the first year, including R$46 billion from foreign investors
register.text: Public money and currency hedges that draw private capital into the bioeconomy, renewable energy, resilient infrastructure and forest restoration. The second auction alone is expected to restore 1.4 million hectares.

register.name: Paraíba Access to Resilient Water and Sanitation Services
register.detail: Announced 22 September 2026 · First phase of the Integrated Water Security Program for Northeast Brazil
register.note: IBRD loan · $23m from the State of Paraíba
register.text: Rehabilitates and expands the wastewater treatment plant of the João Pessoa metropolitan region, which serves about 1.4 million people, and cuts water losses estimated at 45 percent. It prepares a sanitation public-private partnership for about 2 million urban residents in 85 municipalities. It moves shelter, measured by safely managed sanitation, the standard that sets Brazil’s Coverage.

register.name: PPP for the Electrification and Modernization of São Paulo Water Crossings
register.detail: Approved 22 September 2026 · World Bank
register.note: World Bank financing for a public-private partnership
register.text: A World Bank operation approved on 22 September 2026 for a public-private partnership to electrify and modernise São Paulo’s water crossings.

register.name: Decarbonization of Energy-Intensive Value Chains, through BNDES
register.detail: Approved 15 September 2026 · IBRD loan, with $60m from the Clean Technology Fund
register.note: Expected to mobilise $1.8bn of other development and commercial financing
register.text: A US$1 billion IBRD loan and a US$60 million Clean Technology Fund loan, channelled through BNDES, for low-carbon cement, steel, glass, chemicals and aluminium, low-carbon fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel, e-methanol and biomethane, and shared green hydrogen and ammonia infrastructure. It supports Brazil’s target of cutting the greenhouse gas intensity of industrial GDP by 30 percent by 2033.

register.name: Promoting Sustainable Housing in Brazil
register.detail: Approved 31 August 2026 · World Bank
register.note: World Bank financing for sustainable housing
register.text: A World Bank operation approved on 31 August 2026 to promote sustainable housing in Brazil. Shelter, measured by safely managed sanitation, is the standard that sets Brazil’s Coverage.

register.name: Paraná Water Security Project
register.detail: Announced 26 August 2026 · Under the AgriConnect initiative
register.note: IBRD loan
register.text: Strengthens water management with 42 watershed plans, improves water and sanitation for about 60,000 rural residents and water safety for 2.2 million urban residents, and protects about 9,200 farmers against drought and extreme weather. It restores riparian forest on 10,690 hectares. It moves water, food and livelihood among the seven standards.

register.name: Fortaleza fiscal reform and sustainable urban growth
register.detail: Announced 31 July 2026 · Loan to the Municipality of Fortaleza
register.note: IBRD loan
register.text: Supports a new master plan centred on public transport, a municipal climate policy and fiscal reforms to property tax and street lighting. By January 2028 the city targets 237 hectares reserved for social housing, 1,500 housing units improved and 3,000 land titles, at least 60 percent to women. It moves shelter, the standard that sets Brazil’s Coverage.

register.name: São Paulo business reform and jobs
register.detail: Announced 16 July 2026 · Supports the Plano São Paulo na Direção Certa
register.note: World Bank Group
register.text: Finances a statewide job training and matching platform expected to reach 80,000 users, a programme that moves vulnerable residents into formal work, and reforms that unify business registration and licensing and strengthen concessions in transport, energy, water and sanitation. It moves livelihood among the seven standards.

register.name: Northeast energy transition and jobs, through Banco do Nordeste
register.detail: Approved 15 May 2026 · Package of $968M with Clean Technology Fund, Livable Planet Fund and ESMAP
register.note: World Bank loan · Expected to leverage over $423m of commercial financing
register.text: Expands finance through Banco do Nordeste for first-of-a-kind projects in sustainable aviation fuel, low-carbon fertiliser, steel and cement, with the shared infrastructure they need, and grants to build a pipeline of bankable projects. It moves energy and livelihood among the seven standards.

register.name: Bahia infrastructure, digital access and energy
register.detail: Approved 20 March 2026
register.note: World Bank loan
register.text: Supports reforms and investment in road contracting that accounts for climate risk and draws in private capital, public transport and access to jobs, the security of digital public services, and distributed renewable energy in rural areas, including island communities on the São Francisco River. It moves energy and livelihood among the seven standards.

register.name: Accelerating Energy Transition in the Amazon, through Banco da Amazônia
register.detail: Approved 20 March 2026 · Total investment $627.75M
register.note: IBRD loan · $400m from the federal government and $125m commercial financing
register.text: A credit line through Banco da Amazônia for renewable power, grid upgrades and energy efficiency in the Legal Amazon, with an ESMAP grant for technical assistance. It is expected to raise renewable generation, cut diesel use and bring electricity to more than one million residents who lack basic access. It moves energy, the fourth of the seven standards.

register.name: Tocantins jobs, connectivity and rural resilience
register.detail: Approved 27 February 2026 · Eight years
register.note: World Bank loan · $30m from the State of Tocantins
register.text: Rehabilitates and maintains 746 km of paved state roads under performance-based contracts and prepares the state’s first road public-private partnerships. It supports 12,000 family farmers, including women-led, youth, Indigenous and Quilombola producers, and tourism in the Jalapão region. It moves food and livelihood among the seven standards.

register.name: Foreign-exchange hedging facility
register.detail: IDB and the Central Bank of Brazil · Announced at COP30
register.note: Up to $3.4 billion of currency hedging
register.text: Protects foreign investors from swings in the real, the single largest barrier to long-term green investment in Brazil.

register.name: Bahia Sustainable Rural Development Project
register.detail: Approved 7 November 2024 · Investment project financing
register.note: Family farms and rural water
register.text: Raises farm productivity, market access and climate resilience for family farmers, and expands rural water access.

register.name: Bahia Proactive, Safe and Resilient Road Asset Management
register.detail: Approved 10 September 2024 · First part of a $1.662 billion national road programme
register.note: Road rehabilitation, maintenance and city bypasses
register.text: Performance-based contracts to rehabilitate and maintain roads with attention to safety and climate resilience, bypasses around cities on key corridors, and better access to selected rural roads, for 2.35 million people in Bahia.

register.name: Enhancing Prosperity and Sustainability in the State of Sergipe
register.detail: Approved 27 August 2024 · World Bank loan
register.note: Fiscal sustainability and natural resource management
register.text: Supports a new fiscal framework for Sergipe, Brazil’s smallest state by area, with water resource management to build drought resilience, more solar energy and more recycling.

register.name: Pernambuco Rural Water and Sanitation Project
register.detail: Approved 17 May 2024 · Investment project financing
register.note: Rural water and sanitation
register.text: Extends reliable, climate-resilient water and sanitation services to rural communities. Sanitation is how shelter is measured on this page, the standard that sets Brazil’s Coverage.

register.name: State of Ceará Sustainable Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 28 March 2024 · JPY 80.1 billion · 20 years, guaranteed by Brazil
register.note: Public financial management and a clean energy transition
register.text: A loan of JPY 80.1 billion, equivalent to US$541.9 million, to modernise public investment, asset management and internal controls, and to support a fair and clean energy transition, including clean energy skills for vulnerable people.

register.name: Sustainable Human Development Project in the State of Pará
register.detail: Approved 28 March 2024 · Investment project financing
register.note: Human development in the Amazon state
register.text: Investment in human development in Pará, the Amazon state that hosted COP30.

register.name: Mato Grosso Sustainable Development of Family Farming
register.detail: Approved 5 February 2024 · IBRD loan · Six years
register.note: About 15,000 family farmers; $20m from the State of Mato Grosso
register.text: Helps family farmers reach competitive markets, build climate resilience and improve land and environmental management, prioritising Indigenous Peoples, Quilombolas, other traditional communities, women and young people.

register.name: Support to the New Bolsa Família Conditional Cash Transfer Program
register.detail: Approved 6 December 2023 · World Bank project
register.note: About 9 million children in eligible households
register.text: Protects the incomes of poor families with children aged up to six, and restores the school attendance, vaccination and health check-up conditions waived during the pandemic. The World Bank expects about 9 million children to benefit.

register.name: Rio de Janeiro Adjustment and Sustainable Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 16 November 2023 · Second of two operations with the city
register.note: Budget support to the City of Rio de Janeiro
register.text: Supports fiscal accountability, pension management, a low-carbon and climate-resilient revival of downtown Rio by 2030, a better bus rapid transit model, and safer complementary transport in informal settlements.

register.name: Caixa Housing
register.detail: Approved 30 March 2026 · Signed 31 March 2026 · Invested 8 April 2026 · Five years
register.note: IFC senior loan in local currency to Caixa Econômica Federal
register.text: An IFC loan of up to US$200 million equivalent in reais to Caixa Econômica Federal for housing construction certified under Selo Casa Azul + CAIXA and green building standards such as EDGE, LEED and AQUA, and for Caixa’s funding under Eco Invest. It bears on shelter, the standard that sets Brazil’s Coverage.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: About 4.9 million km² of forest, now valued alive by a fund Brazil designed.

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person, 2022
items.text: More fresh water per person than almost any large nation on Earth.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2021
items.text: Rivers, wind and sun already power most of the nation.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: About 2.37 million km² farmed, beside a forest twice its size.

items.name: The Forest Fund
items.label: Committed to the TFFF, Oct 2026
items.text: Launched by Brazil at COP30 in Belém, November 2025, to pay for forest kept standing.
items.alt: Belém, where the Tropical Forest Forever Facility was launched

items.name: Águas do Rio
items.text: Rio’s largest sanitation concession: universal water and 90% sewage collection for 10 million people.

items.name: Vivenda
items.text: Financed home renovations in south São Paulo: more than 2,000 homes for over 6,000 people.

items.name: Revolusolar
items.text: A solar cooperative in the Babilônia and Chapéu Mangueira favelas of Rio, owned by its members.

items.name: dr.consulta
items.text: Affordable clinics in São Paulo: 28 centres and nearly 800,000 patients a year.

items.name: Nubank
items.text: Digital banking that brought 31.5 million previously unbanked Brazilians into the financial system.

coverage.gap_text: Brazilians without a safely managed toilet at home: about one in two.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Fewer than one in ten moderately or severely food insecure, 2024

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: Clean cooking for 97%; electricity use well above 1,000 kWh a person

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 48% of children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school; 2013 data, dated

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$8.30 a day; 20.6% live below it
